column3: “Give a blast on a ram’s horn” is rendered “Blow a trumpet,” and “sound a battle signal” “sound an alarm.”
“Cloud” is rendered “clouds”; NASB supplies “So there is”; “a generation and a generation” is rendered “many generations.”
“Before it … after it” is rendered “before them … behind them”; NASB renders the last line as “nothing at all escapes them.”
“Horsemen” is rendered “war horses.”
“Sound” is rendered “noise” and “crackling”; NASB places “They leap” before “on the tops.”
“Peoples” (plural) is rendered “the people”; “gather a glow” is rendered “turn pale.” The meaning is uncertain.
“Warriors” is rendered “mighty men,” and “men of war” “soldiers”; “each on its ways they go” is rendered “they each march in line.”
“Through the weapons they fall” is rendered “When they burst through the defenses”; “not they stop” is rendered “They do not break ranks.”
“Go up” is rendered “climb,” and “go” “enter.”
“Withdraw” is rendered “lose.”
“Gives forth his voice” is rendered “utters His voice”; NASB renders “for” as “Surely” and “indeed.”
“Wailing” is rendered “mourning.”
“Tear” is rendered “rend”; “long of angers” is rendered “Slow to anger,” “covenant loyalty” “lovingkindness,” and “the harm” “evil”; NASB adds “Now.”
“Who knows he will turn” is rendered “Who knows whether He will not turn”; “drink offering” is rendered “libation,” and NASB adds “Even.”
“Give a blast on a ram’s horn” is rendered “Blow a trumpet,” and “call an assembly” “proclaim a solemn assembly.”
“Consecrate an assembly” is rendered “sanctify the congregation”; “suckling-children of breasts” is rendered “nursing infants,” and “chamber” “bridal chamber.”
“Servants” is rendered “ministers,” and “have compassion” “Spare”; “to mock on them” is rendered “A byword.”
The Hebrew past “became jealous … had compassion” is rendered as future, “will be zealous … will have pity.”
The Hebrew past “answered” is rendered “will answer”; NASB adds “in full” and “never.”
“The northerner” is rendered “the northern army,” “its face” “its vanguard,” and “its end” “its rear guard”; NASB renders “he has made great to do” as “it has done great things.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Given their strength” is rendered “yielded in full.”
“People of Zion” is rendered “sons of Zion”; “the early rain for righteousness” is rendered “the early rain for your vindication,” and “in the first” “as before.”
NASB renders “wine-vats” as “vats.”
The Hebrew order of locust names differs from 1:4; NASB uses “swarming,” “creeping,” “stripping,” and “gnawing.” “Restore” is rendered “make up to you.”
“Eat completely and being satisfied” is rendered “have plenty to eat and be satisfied”; “wonderfully” is rendered “wondrously,” and NASB adds “Then.”
“There is not yet” is rendered “there is no other”; NASB adds “Thus.”
MT 3:1. “After thus” is rendered “after this,” and “all flesh” “all mankind”; NASB capitalizes “Spirit.”
MT 3:2. NASB capitalizes “Spirit.”
MT 3:3. “Heavens” is rendered “sky,” and “put” “display.”
